html:
SMTO-FIL-0038 — The copied file didn't match the original, so it wasn't saved

GUID: e066cf77-e51c-46c9-aa74-5dc87900bee6
Slug: file-transfer-hash-mismatch
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • At the end of a copy between Gateways, SMTO compared the received file with the original and found they were different. SMTO did not put the mismatched file in place at the destination.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the drive that receives the file on the destination computer isn't full or reporting errors. A full or failing drive can change data as it is written, which is what this check caught.
  2. Make sure no program is still writing to the original file during the copy. A file that changes partway through won't match what was sent.
  3. Ask SMTO in the conversation to show the size and last-modified time of the file at the destination and of the original file, and compare them. If the destination file is already there and matches, the copy doesn't need to be repeated.
  4. Only if the destination file is missing or still the old version, ask SMTO to copy the file again. A fresh copy is checked the same way, so only a file that matches the original is saved.

What success looks like

  • The new copy finishes and SMTO reports the file was copied and verified.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the destination Gateway. If the mismatch happens again, don't keep repeating the copy; the drive or connection needs to be checked first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Before publication, the destination Gateway's recomputed SHA-256 of the staged .smto-transfer-*.partial file differed from the digest the controller computed while relaying, so destination_commit refused to publish.

What this means

  • The staged destination's computed SHA-256 differs from the commit request's expected digest before publication. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The staged destination's computed SHA-256 differs from the commit request's expected digest before publication.

How to diagnose it

  • Keep the stage untrusted and inspect original source identity, expected digest and cleanup receipt.

How to fix it

  • Abort or settle the original stage (destination_abort or destination_reconcile for the transfer_id) and confirm cleanup_complete, then check destination storage health (kernel log, SMART, free space) and both Gateways' logs and versions. Start a new copy only after the original transfer is settled; this attempt did not replace the destination path.
  • Settle or abort the original stage through the supported flow, then transfer authoritative content under a new authorized operation if needed.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • A settled supported transfer publishes only content whose final size and digest match.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
